content.text: Valid, and it's the third instance of this exact drift class today: a doc that restates config, contradicting it eight lines from my own new section. Let me see it:

result.output:
### Turbo task graph

`turbo.json` defines three tasks. Each task runs only in workspace members that declare the matching `package.json` script — there is no global config to update when you add a new member.

| Task        | `inputs`                                                                 | Cached?             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| `typecheck` | `action.yml`, `*.ts`, `src/**/*.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`     | Yes                 |
| `test`      | `*.ts`, `src/**/*.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json` (no `action.yml`) | Yes                 |
| `clean`     | _none_                                                                   | No (`cache: false`) |

`action.yml` is intentionally excluded from `test` inputs — changes to action metadata invalidate `typecheck` but not the test cache. If you add a task that needs cache-aware action-metadata sensitivity, include `action.yml` in its `inputs`.

### Per-member docs and agent files

Any action or package directory (TypeScript action, YAML composite action, or package) MAY include:

content.text: Guard fixed and now genuinely bites — reverting the table row fails 6 assertions. Squashing into the commit and replying:

input.command:
cd /Users/tony_vi/.warp/worktrees/code-assistants/chamisa-badger
R=awinogradov/code-assistants
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tony-vi--warp-worktrees-code-assistants-chamisa-badger/a0f2285c-709e-4de2-9866-569a01e1e104/scratchpad
OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cat > "$SP/i-turbo.txt" <<'EOF'
fix(turbo): take markdown as an input to the test task

- Add root-relative globs for claude-plugins, docs, rfc, rules and the
  root README and CONTRIBUTING to the test task inputs
- Without them a docs-only change was a cache hit, so the guards that
  assert markdown never ran on the change most likely to break them
- Record the reasoning in the workspace doc, since turbo.json is strict
  JSON and cannot carry a comment
- Update the task-graph table row to match the new inputs
- Add turboInputsDocSync.test.ts pinning that row against turbo.json
EOF
bunx --no -- commitlint < "$SP/i-turbo.txt" >/dev/null && echo "commitlint OK"
git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git add -A
git commit -F "$SP/i-turbo.txt" --quiet 2>&1 | grep -vE '^\[(STARTED|COMPLETED|SKIPPED)\]' | tail -1
echo "✓ $(git log -1 --format=%s)"
git diff --stat $OLD..HEAD
git push --force-with-lease origin maintenance-turbo-test-markdown-inputs 2>&1 | tail -1
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cat > "$SP/r511.md" <<EOF
Fixed in [${SHA:0:7}](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/commit/$SHA) — and I pinned it, because this is the third time today the same shape has bitten.

The row now lists the \`\$TURBO_ROOT\$\` globs. But the underlying problem is that the table restates \`turbo.json\`, and a second copy nobody re-reads drifts: the same class produced the chapter 5 field-list drift on #499 and the chapter 5 score-line drift on #503. So \`turboInputsDocSync.test.ts\` now reads \`turbo.json\` and asserts the table row names every input, root-relative ones included.

Writing that guard immediately caught a bug in itself, which is worth recording. My first version searched the whole chapter for a \`| \\\`test\\\` |\` row — but the Workspace-scripts table has one too, and it appears earlier, so the assertions were checking a row that never mentions inputs at all. It failed six ways on the correct documentation. Scoping the search to the \`### Turbo task graph\` section first fixed it, and reverting your finding now fails six assertions as it should.

The check is loose about glob syntax and strict about coverage — it asserts the directory or filename each input targets appears in the row, so rewording the row is fine but dropping an input is not.
EOF
body=$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.dumps({'body':open(sys.argv[1]).read()}))" "$SP/r511.md")
printf '%s' "$body" | gh api -X POST "repos/$R/issues/511/comments" --input - --jq '"✓ commented -> \(.html_url)"'
